---
type: parens
title: 'Make it equal $x^2$'
expression: − 1 · x · − 1 + x + 2 − 2 − 1
target: x²
---

Tap a gap to place **(**, then a gap to its right to place **)**. Put **one** pair of parentheses in the expression so that it equals $x^2$ for **every** $x$.

## Hint
$x^2 = x \cdot x$. The expression already has one factor $x$ at the start. Can a group of the other terms equal $x$?

## Hint
Look at $1 + x + 2 - 2 - 1$. What does it simplify to? A minus sign in front of a group, $-(\dots)$, takes the opposite of the whole group.

## Solution
**Answer:** $-1 \cdot x \cdot -(1 + x + 2 - 2 - 1)$

The parentheses start **between** the minus sign and the $1$, so the minus sign applies to the whole group:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    -1 \cdot x \cdot -(1 + x + 2 - 2 - 1) &= -1 \cdot x \cdot -(x) \\
                                          &= (-1) \cdot (-1) \cdot x \cdot x \\
                                          &= x^2
\end{aligned}
$$

- **$-1 \cdot x \cdot (-1 + x + 2 - 2 - 1)$**: the group is $x - 2$, so this is $-x(x - 2) = -x^2 + 2x$.
- **$(-1 \cdot x \cdot -1 + x) + 2 - 2 - 1$**: parentheses around a part that is already done first change nothing: it still equals $2x - 1$.
